outcome: adherence to referral advice after a positive PPD screening result
cohort: The study included 1109 women who had a positive Postpartum Depression (PPD) screening result (EPDS score >= 10) from an initial cohort of 9161 women who took part in a midwife-led PPD screening.
finding: Only 8% (85 of 1109) of referred mothers enrolled in psychological consultations, with predictors of seeking help including higher EPDS scores, higher gestational age at birth, fewer children, C-section experience, a self-assessed good financial situation, and a postgraduate higher education degree.
mod_finding: C-section experience was identified as a predictor for mothers seeking psychological help after a positive PPD screening.
cross-section timing: Postpartum (timing within postpartum period not specified)
gest_age: Higher gestational age at birth was a predictor of seeking help.
